referenced_urls.title: Small agents should know what their tools do

relevance: Makes small local models far safer and more efficient tool users.

media.description: Abstract excerpt introducing EffectWorld, effect-typed tools that let a replay verifier check effect safety; LoRA adapters lift Qwen3-4B task success from 53% to 99% in distribution.
media.ocr_text: Small open language models can call tools, but they do not reason about what a call does: they delete without asking, repeat writes, re-read state they already hold, and issue one call per turn where a short program would do. We introduce EffectWorld, an executable world of effect-typed tools in which every tool declares its effect, whether it is idempotent, and which resources it reads and writes. These declarations let a replay verifier decide whether a trace is effect-safe without labels or judge models, let an executor run tool programs of several dependent calls in one turn, and let a compiler-style optimizer turn wasteful traces into verified training signal; together they make EffectWorld a benchmark of effect safety and call efficiency. Low-rank adapters trained on this data deliver large gains: on Qwen3-4B, they raise task success from 53% to 99% in distribution, from 52% to 81% on a held-out…
